title.narrative: Promoting biodiversity conservation and resilience in the GCC and Yemen

description.narrative: The Gulf region and Yemen hosts a variety of different, yet very similar, ecosystems and habitats, home to unique and very rich fauna and flora. However, biodiversity hotspots in the region are facing numerous threats, evident in the loss of ecosystems, depletion of flora and fauna, including endemic species, genetic erosion, desertification, the proliferation of invasive species and diseases, pollution, and contamination, among other challenges. These threats are often exacerbated by lack of awareness and community engagement, weak institutional capacities, a lack of comprehensive data and accurate information, social pressures, and increased demand on natural resources due to growing population. The impact of climate change further exacerbates the challenges, hampering Member Sates' ability to mitigate and recover from socio-economic and environmental losses. The workplan proposed to address some of these challenges through enhanced cooperation amongst different stakeholders, advancing scientific research and strengthening biodiversity conservation efforts.
